description: We’re two first-year university students, one studying Mathematics and Computer science and the other Engineering. We're best friends and decided to work on a project focused on farming and agriculture. We're looking for motivated people who are interested in the topic and can bring  different skills, ideas and perspectives to the team. We're open to anyone interested in coding, engineering, agriculture or design!
summary:
'Soil Memory' is a satellite-driven soil health monitoring and crop-rotation planning tool designed to help Moroccan farmers make more sustainable agricultural decisions.

Using NASA MODIS vegetation indices (NDVI) and NASA SMAP soil moisture data, the platform analyzes historical satellite observations to identify changes in vegetation health and soil moisture across five Moroccan agricultural regions: Doukkala, Tadla, Souss, El Haouz, and Gharb.

Beyond monitoring current soil conditions, Soil Memory offers an interactive crop-rotation planner that compares six-year scenarios based on soil organic matter, nitrogen, irrigation pressure, crop suitability, and disease risk.

Designed with accessibility in mind, the application features an Arabic and English interface, voice-assisted results, and simple traffic-light indicators that translate complex satellite data into understandable insights.

By bridging the gap between Earth observation data and everyday farming decisions, Soil Memory aims to make satellite-powered agricultural insights more accessible and encourage informed, sustainable soil management.
details:
What it does

Soil Memory turns NASA Earthdata satellite observations into a simple answer for farmers: is my soil getting better or worse, and which crop rotation is best for it? A farmer taps their field on a satellite map. The app compares recent NASA MODIS vegetation and SMAP soil moisture with earlier years, and shows two traffic lights that it reads aloud in Arabic or English. In the Rotation Lab, the farmer compares two 3-crop plans from 33 local crops. The app shows how each plan affects soil organic matter, nitrogen, disease risk and irrigation pressure over 6 years.

Benefits and impact

Satellite data is usually made for scientists. Soil Memory makes it usable for farmers, with no charts to read, a voice readout and a full Arabic interface. It helps farmers in Morocco see slow soil decline early and choose more sustainable rotations before planting.

Tools

Python, Streamlit, pandas, Folium, Esri satellite imagery, gTTS, and NASA MODIS and SMAP data. It runs in any web browser.

DATA AND PLATFORMS

- NASA MODIS Terra MOD13Q1 v6.1 (vegetation index, NDVI, 250 m, 16-day)

- NASA SMAP L4 SPL4SMGP v8 (surface soil moisture, 9 km, 3-hourly)

- Google Earth Engine (used to access and average the NASA datasets)

- Google Colab (Python notebook used to download and process the data)

- Esri World Imagery (satellite background map, visual only)

SOFTWARE

- Python, pandas

- Streamlit and Streamlit Community Cloud (app and hosting)

- folium and streamlit-folium (interactive satellite map)

- gTTS, Google Text-to-Speech (Arabic audio)

- GitHub (code hosting)

AI TOOLS

- Claude (Anthropic): used for coding, planning and prototyping. It helped write the app code, structure the data pipeline and design the Arabic interface and rotation simulator. The team ran the data processing, tested the app, chose the regions and crops, and reviewed the results.

- Clueso (AI video tool): used to produce the demo video.

Creativity

It puts satellite monitoring and a “what if” rotation planner in one simple screen. It is Arabic-first, with right-to-left layout, voice output and traffic lights instead of dashboards. It also handles real farming details: legume nitrogen credits, monoculture penalties, permanent tree crops and regional crop suitability.

What we considered

Farmers with limited literacy or connectivity, language access, and local crops and regional conditions across five Moroccan regions.
